definition: A body that moves freely after it has been launched, with no engine or push, so the only forces on it are its weight and any fluid resistance.
The force a gas or liquid exerts on a body moving through it, acting opposite to the body's velocity relative to the fluid and increasing with speed; air resistance and drag are examples.
The constant speed of a body falling through a fluid once the fluid resistance plus any upthrust balances its weight, so the resultant force and the acceleration are zero (the body is still moving).
